team: Andrea Cutroni, Rania Chihaoui, Symon Kipekemi
faculty: Lucia Leva Fuentes, James McBennett, Laukik Lad
description: A computational approach to Jakarta's flood resilience, using rule-based aggregation to merge housing, public programs and a stadium.
body: Floating Grounds explores how large-scale infrastructure can support community life while addressing land subsidence, flooding, and environmental stress through modular, floating architecture.

Powered by the WASP plug-in, the Grasshopper workflow generates a responsive design that adapts to the site conditions and runs environmental and structural analysis. A standardized 5 × 5 m grid, lightweight timber and floating pontoons, improve construction efficiency, reduce carbon impact and ensure stability via Archimede's principle.
The project follows a parametric, bottom-up approach and data-driven workflow ensuring sustainable, scalable solutions for flood-prone cities.

sections.title: Workflow
body: Three programs run as parallel tracks through a single Grasshopper definition. Each is driven by its own inputs, orientation logic and geometry rules, then converges on one WASP aggregation step before environmental and structural analysis feed back into the result.

sections.title: Step by Step
body: Each of the three programs is built up through its own ordered sequence of moves, all of them sharing the same floating platform and the same 5 × 5 m module.

scenes.title: Kit of Parts
scenes.caption: The modules WASP aggregates, grouped by zone. Modules include residential units, circulation, cores, workshops, coworking spaces, and service areas.

scenes.title: Topology
scenes.caption: The adjacency rules binding those modules — stadium units read from pitch to exterior, while buffer-zone and residential program is sorted by the level it can occupy: ground, ground-to-upper, or upper only.

scenes.title: Stadium
scenes.caption: Any waterfront → flood resistance → S-N pitch orientation → create offset → modular stands

scenes.title: Buffer Zone
scenes.caption: Create cores → GF aggregation → FX aggregation

scenes.title: Residential
scenes.caption: Floating platform & start points → opening the ecosystem plazas → creating core and circulations → run aggregation

sections.title: Bowl Creation
body: Stadium seating was generated from FIFA sightline guidance rather than drawn. A target C-value of 90 mm drives a multi-tier 2D profile, which is swept along the bowl plan to produce the seating mesh and the spectator eyepoints used to verify every row.

scenes.title: C-Value
scenes.caption: The vertical clearance between a spectator's sightline to the field and the eye level of the person in front. 90 mm was taken as the target.

scenes.title: Parameters
scenes.caption: Pitch and tier inputs driving the bowl — dimensions, corner radius, row count, row width and seat spacing.

scenes.title: Generation
scenes.caption: The multi-tier profile is swept along the bowl plan, then spectator eyepoints are picked and evaluated row by row.

sections.title: Structural & Environmental Analysis
body: Energy modelling started from a single residential unit — a WWR × orientation sweep establishing that south and east glazing minimise annual loads — then scaled to the full masterplan. Structurally, a timber frame was compared against concrete and steel, verified in FEM, and its support reactions sized the pontoons through Archimedes' principle.

scenes.title: Base Scenario
scenes.caption: Annual loads swept across window-to-wall ratio and orientation. South and east glazing minimise the total.

scenes.title: Design Scenario
scenes.caption: Monthly load intensity, daily peak load and incident radiation for a 25 m² residential unit.

scenes.title: Photovoltaics
scenes.caption: Roof-mounted monocrystalline modules at 20% rated efficiency, offsetting half the unit's cooling load.

scenes.title: Masterplan Yield
scenes.caption: Radiation across the full aggregation — 779,140 kWh of on-site production, 38% of the cooling load.

scenes.title: Façade Radiation
scenes.caption: Average façade radiation falls from 830 to 564 kWh/m² once the massing is aggregated rather than boxed.

scenes.title: Material Choice
scenes.caption: Concrete, steel and timber compared by weight and embodied carbon. Timber wins on both counts.

scenes.title: FEM Displacement
scenes.caption: Three-storey timber frame under 2 kN/m² dead and live load, peaking at 1.57 mm.

scenes.title: Buoyancy
scenes.caption: Support reactions of 360.6 kN sized through Archimedes' principle to a 1.5 m immersed depth.

sections.title: Testing
body: The definition was re-run against different scenarios and site locations from identical inputs — 29,250 m² of site at FAR 1, with 593 residential, 143 commercial and 63 stadium parts available — to see how stable the result stays. The residential part count settles at 625 every time; what moves is the built area and the commercial mix.

scenes.title: Scenarios
scenes.caption: 11,000 m² of residential built area across 625 parts, with 3,300 m² of commercial across 106.

scenes.title: Location 1
scenes.caption: 10,650 m² of residential across the same 625 parts, trading floor area for a slightly larger commercial band — 3,350 m² across 108.

sections.title: Drawings
body: The aggregation resolves into a 29,250 m² lot holding 540 residents and a stadium capacity of 1,620, organized on a 45 m structural grid.

scenes.title: Masterplan
scenes.caption: Roof plan on the 45 m grid, the stadium anchored to the shoreline and housing spreading north over the water.

scenes.title: Ground Floor
scenes.caption: Ground level — stands, service cores and the open deck that carries the residential blocks.

scenes.title: Conceptual Section
scenes.caption: Long section through stand, buffer zone and housing, cut on the 5 m module.

scenes.title: Aggregation
scenes.caption: Programme distribution across the aggregation, with the full area schedule and occupancy figures.

scenes.title: Programme by Floor
scenes.caption: Ground, first and second floors colour-coded by use across the whole site.

scenes.title: Residential Block
scenes.caption: One block resolved floor by floor — workshop units at grade, R1 and R2 apartments above.
